clue.text: Mechanic producing a terrific explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the words a terrific apart so their letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic sets off a huge bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' is the anagram signal: the letters of A TERRIFIC are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman, especially a military or naval engineering technician.

clue.text: Crewman on vessel without a superior

indicators.note: in a down clue the crewman sits on top of the vessel word, so comes first

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a member of a ship's crew

indicators.note: without tells us the word a is taken out of the vessel word

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor finds himself aboard a ship with nobody in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves BOT (BOAT less A). 'superior' looks like an adjective but is the noun: the head of a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a monastery is its superior, the title given to an abbot.

clue.text: Author's play appearing after place in series is taken up

definitions.note: read as 'Author is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the play word comes after the reversed piece
in a down clue, taken up means the word is lifted and read from bottom to top

parts.note: a slot is a place in a sequence or schedule
to toy is to play

explanation.surface: A writer's drama is staged after its scheduled slot is booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' makes TOLS in a down entry. 'Author's' reads as 'Author is', so the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy, the Russian novelist of War and Peace, is a famous writer.

clue.text: Explorer's little boy taken in by admiral

definitions.note: read as 'Explorer is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the boy is held inside the admiral's name

parts.note: Jacky Fisher was a famous British admiral, First Sea Lord
Rob is a short form of Robert, a boy's name

explanation.surface: An explorer's young son is deceived by a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' marks the container. Jacky Fisher was a British First Sea Lord; Martin Frobisher an Elizabethan seeking the Northwest Passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Martin Frobisher was a 16th-century English navigator who voyaged to Arctic Canada.

clue.text: Unable to face endless silly chat

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are jumbled foolishly into a new order
endless says the last letter of face is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone too shy to confront others keeps babbling foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims FACE to FAC; 'silly' then rearranges UNABLE TO FAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To confabulate is to talk together informally, a formal word for a natter.

clue.text: Lack of excitement? Not for stag

definitions.text: Lack of excitement? Not for stag

parts.words: Lack of excitement? Not for stag
parts.note: a dull routine is a groove one is stuck in, but the same word for a deer means its mating season, hardly unexciting

explanation.surface: Boredom is not something a male deer suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means a monotonous routine, but for a stag it is the autumn breeding season, so 'Not for stag' plays on the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a tedious unchanging routine; for deer it is the annual breeding period.

clue.text: Premier duke concealing king

indicators.note: the duke word hides the king inside itself

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A leading aristocrat is hiding the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts R inside FIST. 'Duke' is slang for a fist, as in 'put up your dukes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier and first both mean foremost or top-ranking.

clue.text: Put on act willingly? So it was said

indicators.note: points to the spoken form, the word for willingly sounding like the entry

parts.note: fain is an old word meaning gladly or willingly

explanation.surface: Was the performance voluntary? That was the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So it was said' signals a sound-alike: FAIN, archaic for 'gladly', is said like FEIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to pretend, to put on a show of something not felt.

clue.text: Jazz season covered by newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue the season word sits beneath the newspaper word

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper
a season is a period, a time

explanation.surface: The jazz festival season is reported in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'covered by' puts TIME below RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style that was a forerunner of jazz.

clue.text: One who bedevils people in high places

indicators.note: the people word goes inside the pair of high places

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops, so two high places are two tors
men are people

explanation.surface: A tormenting figure persecutes those living up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' needs the plural 'high places' read as two tors, rocky hilltops typical of Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor torments, harassing and plaguing others as a devil would.

clue.text: Sky delivery, with all-rounder bowling

parts.note: in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled
the letter O is round all the way
in cricket a bowler who is bowling is said to be on

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bats and bowls sends down a high ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-rounder' pretends to be a cricketer who bats and bowls; it is the round letter O. 'Sky' is a verb: to hit a ball high.
explanation.definitionFit: To sky a ball and to balloon it both mean to hit it high into the air.

clue.text: Set off and run into bouncy character

indicators.note: the run letter is placed inside the character's name

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncing tiger in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jumpy figure is startled and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside TIGGER, the bouncing tiger of the Pooh stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to start it off or provoke it.

clue.text: All the players scored

parts.note: a marking in a musical score telling the whole orchestra to play together

explanation.surface: Every member of the team got points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' seems to be about sport, but it means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the Italian direction in music for the full ensemble to perform.

clue.text: Like a metal entering a different state

indicators.note: being put in a different state means the letters of entering a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something silvery passes into a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different state' signals an anagram of ENTERING A; 'state' tempts one to think of the country, Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine as an adjective means silvery, from the Latin argentum for silver.

clue.text: Novel sort of enlargement

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to rearrange, so the letters of enlargement are sorted

explanation.surface: A new kind of expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective, but it is the definition: John Buchan's 1916 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenmantle is a spy novel by John Buchan featuring Richard Hannay.

clue.text: Make fun of medical philanthropist

definitions.meaning: Thomas ..., the 18th-century benefactor who founded ... Hospital in London

explanation.surface: Ridicule a man who gave money to medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy is to ridicule; Thomas Guy founded a famous London hospital.

clue.text: Sage in a jar

definitions.meaning: a large stoneware drinking jug or flagon decorated with a bearded face

explanation.surface: A wise herb kept in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wise man with a white beard is a greybeard, as is a bellarmine stoneware flask.

clue.text: Restrictive measure to take in a ringleader and others

parts.note: to house someone is to take them in and shelter them
the leading letter of ring
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Police act to detain a gang leader and his accomplices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' means the first letter of RING. The surface of police rounding up a gang is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: House arrest confines someone to their home, a restraint imposed by authorities.

clue.text: Knocking into shape in bloody battle

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
action is fighting, combat

explanation.surface: Getting troops into order during a gory fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is editing, preparing a text for publication by revising it.

clue.text: Affected by diversion, ain't put out — started going round

indicators.note: the started word wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: entered can mean began or embarked on

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of ain't are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by a distraction began to turn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' scrambles the letters of ain't; 'going round' has the started word enclose them. The surface's diversion is a distraction, not a detour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entertained is to be amused, kept happy by an amusement.

clue.text: It's displayed frontally in vehicle, namely as legal requirement

definitions.text: It's displayed frontally in vehicle, namely as legal requirement

indicators.note: the front letter goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle

indicators.note: only the front letter of displayed is used

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely

explanation.surface: Something shown at the front of a car, as the law demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frontally' picks D; 'in' sets it inside the vehicle. A British tax disc, proof of paid road tax, had to be shown on the windscreen until 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax disc was a circular licence that had to be shown on British vehicles.

clue.text: Salt produced using most of acid

indicators.note: most of says the acid word loses its final letter

parts.note: tart means sour, acid in taste

explanation.surface: A salt is formed from an acid in a chemistry lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TART to TAR. 'Salt' looks chemical but means an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and tar are both informal words for a sailor.

clue.text: Wine and brandy, for example, 14 ac gets attached to

parts.note: tent is a dark red Spanish wine
a peg is a drink of spirits, such as brandy and soda

explanation.surface: Drinks to which a man gets attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across is GUY, here a guy rope; a tent peg holds it down.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope is fastened to the ground by a pegging spike.

clue.text: Producer of old pictures appeared with artist on TV

indicators.note: in an across entry the appeared and artist words come after the TV word

parts.note: the box is slang for television
came means turned up, appeared
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An old film-maker appeared on television with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sends the later pieces after the TV word in an across entry; a Royal Academician is the crossword's usual artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early photographic device.

clue.text: Imitation piano in mountain-top home

indicators.note: the piano letter sits inside the nest word

parts.note: an aery or eyrie is an eagle's nest high on a mountain
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A fake piano in an alpine chalet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside AERY, a variant spelling of eyrie.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is mimicry, copying others as an ape is thought to.

clue.text: Leaving tail off fish

indicators.note: tail off means the fish word loses its last letter

parts.note: the conger is a large sea eel

explanation.surface: Departing after chopping the end off a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' trims CONGER to CONGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A congé is a formal leave-taking or dismissal.

clue.text: Wader in water, gently rising

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird stands in water that slowly rises.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'rising' reads the run TERGE, inside 'water, gently', upwards; 'in' marks the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like bird that wades in shallows.

clue.text: Sweet flavour is filling a requirement

indicators.note: the word is fills the gap inside the requirement phrase

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A sweet flavour satisfies a necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' marks the container; 'Sweet' is a noun-like adjective tempting one towards confectionery rather than the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed has a liquorice taste and flavours sweets.

clue.text: Party split by an upstart or two

indicators.note: the party word is broken open by the other letter

parts.note: a do is a party
the starting letter of up

explanation.surface: A party is divided by one or two newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstart' gives the start of UP, U; 'split by' puts it in DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, a couple.

clue.text: One in danger of falling for a holiday-maker

definitions.meaning: someone who stumbles or catches a foot

explanation.surface: Someone at risk of a fall falls for a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trips may fall; a tripper is also an excursionist.

clue.text: Birdie — below par

definitions.meaning: a ...-bird, a child's word for a small bird

explanation.surface: A golfer scores one under par.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicky-bird is nursery talk for a bird; dicky also means weak or unsound.

clue.text: By appearing in public, such a sudden success?

definitions.text: By appearing in public, such a sudden success?

parts.words: By appearing in public, such a sudden success?
parts.note: a performer who makes a debut and is famous by next morning has a sudden success of this kind

explanation.surface: Does going public bring instant stardom?
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight success is one achieved suddenly, seemingly in a single night.
